messages:
maya: heads-up — gitops helm lint is failing on staging for the gpu pool rollout, started after the values change this morning

jamal: saw the CI run, looks like the values schema validation error is: "/workloads/0/batchPolicy: additionalProperties not allowed" but batchPolicy is used in other charts fine? :thinking:

olga: can you paste the portion of values.yaml that triggers it? also which helm-lint version is the pipeline using? we had a difference in v3.10 vs v3.11 earlier that changed some schema handling

maya: here it is:
```yaml
workloads:
  - name: trainer
    gpu:
      type: a100
      count: 2
    batchPolicy: best_effort
    nodeSelector: null  # intentionally letting cluster decide
```

maya: pipeline output snippet:
```
Error: values.schema.json: /workloads/0: invalid object, additionalProperties ["batchPolicy"] not allowed
helm template failed with exit code 1
```

jamal: ah, our values.schema.json for this chart has a strict "properties" list for workload objects. batchPolicy was intentionally left out; previously we had a helper that injected default batching at render-time, but the new change wants batchPolicy in values to control autoscaler hints

liam: fwiw adding it to schema is fine. question: do we want batchPolicy to accept both string and object? ops wants a simple enum ("best_effort", "bounded") but runtime wants an object for "bounded" with maxTokens

olga: recommend union type via anyOf in the schema: oneOf: [{type: string, enum: [...]}, {type: object, properties: {maxTokens: {type: integer}}}] but the linter we run (helm-values-lint action) flags oneOf/anyOf inconsistently unless we pin the validator version

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: lint job failed for PR #4823 (branch: feature/gpu-batching) — see https://ci.internal/build/4823

maya: also seeing a templating runtime edge: in helpers/_batching.tpl we do `{{- default "best_effort" .values.workload.batchPolicy }}` but when .values.workload is null it renders and returns string, whereas other helpers expect map and call `.maxTokens` causing template panic in older helm versions

jamal: so two problems: schema strictness + helper logic that doesn't guard nil maps. I can update helper to coerce with safe-coalesce pattern: `{{- $bp := .Values.workloads | index 0 | default dict }}{{- $bp := $bp.batchPolicy | default "best_effort" }}` — but indexing without guard can also panic if workloads is empty

olga: suggestion: change helpers to use `hasKey` / `kindIs` checks and make the schema accept either string or object. Also update our gitops pipeline to run `helm template --validate=false` in a follow-up job to catch template panics separately from schema issues

liam: operational concern: if chart allows "bounded" as object we need to ensure infer autoscaler mapping to node pools: gpuPoolSelector currently maps type->nodePool. If someone sets bounded with maxTokens=1e6, autoscaler may schedule many pods => GPU capacity spike and cost blowout. We need quota guardrails in pipeline (denylist) or cost-annotation check

maya: good point. we should add a lint rule in our custom checks: when workload.gpu.count > 4 and batchPolicy is bounded with maxTokens > 500k then fail CI with recommendation to open capacity request ticket. That prevents silent cost spikes in prod regions with limited GPUs

jamal: I'll open a small PR to: (1) extend values.schema.json to accept string|object for batchPolicy, (2) update helpers to nil-safe access, (3) add a unit test in chart-testing for the empty-workloads case, (4) add a cost-guard check in our pipeline. Should have it by EOD 

olga: thanks. also bump helm-lint action to pinned v0.5.2 in .github/workflows/chart-lint.yml — add a note in the PR about why (we saw differing anyOf behaviour across patch versions)

maya: quick mitigation: I reverted the chart change on staging so deploys are green, leaving the PR blocked until the schema + helper fix is merged. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: :information_source: rollout reverted (staging) by maya — see https://ci.internal/deploys/8821

liam: when we merge, let's also add a short runbook note in infra-runbooks/gpu-capacity.md about bounded batchPolicy and autoscaler interplay so SRE knows to watch nodepool scale events in eu-west-1

maya: yep, I'll add the runbook blurb and link the PR in the runbook. thanks all!
